insight: Both Matthew 28:19 and Mark 16:15-16 issue the Great Commission to Jesus' disciples, emphasizing the universal scope of their mission to reach all nations or all the world. Each passage uses the aorist participle 'having gone,' underscoring the necessity and decisiveness of active obedience in going forth. Matthew highlights making disciples through teaching and baptizing in the triune name, revealing the Trinitarian foundation of Christian identity, while Mark focuses on the authoritative preaching of the gospel to every creature, stressing proclamation of salvation through Christ. Together, they complement each other by linking the call to go with both the public identification in Christ and the proclamation of the gospel message.
